articles.title: Starlink Offers Resiliency Over Speed for Remote Areas
articles.summary: Satellite internet provides reliable connectivity in areas with limited landline infrastructure.
articles.content: A unique advantage of satellite internet has been identified that sets it apart from traditional providers. This perk is particularly relevant for individuals living in remote areas where access to landline internet services may be scarce or unreliable. In countries like the US, UK, and Canada, many communities have at least some basic landline option available, making it less likely for residents to choose satellite internet as a primary means of connectivity. However, there are certain situations where this type of service can prove to be invaluable. For instance, individuals who value resiliency over raw speed may find that satellite internet is the better choice. This adaptability is inherent in Starlink's design and could potentially save users from difficulties that arise when traditional internet services fail. The ability to access the internet virtually anywhere in the world is a significant benefit of satellite internet. When choosing the right plan, such as one of the various $55 options available, consumers can expect reliable connectivity even in areas with limited or no landline infrastructure. One key aspect that remains unclear until further research is done is exactly how Starlink's speeds compare to those offered by traditional providers. Understanding this will be crucial for making an informed decision about whether satellite internet is right for individual needs. Starlink's network is comprised of clusters of small satellites placed in low Earth orbit (LEO), providing a robust and redundant system for internet connectivity. With over 11,000 operational satellites as of October 2026, covering altitudes ranging from approximately 205 to 311 miles (330 to nearly 500 kilometers), the chances of a single satellite malfunction bringing down the entire network are slim. This redundancy is one of Starlink's most significant advantages over traditional internet connections. If one satellite in a cluster fails, another can take its place, minimizing downtime and ensuring continuous access. Even obstacles such as hills or buildings that might block signals from individual satellites are less likely to cause issues due to the presence of multiple satellites with viable angles. The sheer number of satellites in orbit is also set to increase, with SpaceX's recent application to operate up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites pending approval by the US Federal Communications Commission. This expansion will further enhance coverage and redundancy, making Starlink an increasingly reliable option for internet access. The cluster approach allows for more flexibility in positioning dishes, as there is often a satellite with a clear line of sight available even when obstacles are present. This can be particularly beneficial in areas where traditional internet connections are unreliable or unavailable. As the number of satellites in orbit continues to grow, so too does Starlink's potential for providing bulletproof internet access, assuming power outages and other rare disruptions are accounted for. With the right equipment and setup, users could enjoy virtually uninterrupted connectivity, making it an attractive option for those seeking a reliable internet solution. The Starlink satellite internet system boasts impressive resilience in theory, with its current-generation dishes capable of withstanding extreme temperatures and harsh weather conditions. These models can melt snow and endure temperatures ranging from -40 to 110 degrees Fahrenheit (-40 to 43 degrees Celsius), making them suitable for areas with varying climates. Additionally, when properly mounted, they are designed to withstand heavy rain and winds exceeding 99 miles per hour (about 160 kilometers per hour). However, in reality, Starlink's performance may not always live up to these expectations. Although the system can switch between satellites seamlessly, there can be brief disruptions while this process occurs, causing temporary connectivity issues. Furthermore, prolonged outages are still a possibility due to various factors such as extreme weather, systemic problems on Starlink's end, or issues with local ground-based infrastructure. For some users, these limitations may make Starlink an unattractive option, particularly for those requiring high-speed and low-latency internet connections. Real-time activities like online gaming can be severely impacted by momentary signal disruptions, which can have significant consequences in competitive games such as Fortnite or Counter-Strike. A split second of lag can mean the difference between success and failure. Ultimately, while Starlink offers a unique solution for those seeking reliable internet access in remote areas, its limitations may outweigh its benefits for some users, particularly those with demanding online requirements. articles.title: Hard Disk Drives Show High Failure Rate Within First Year of Operation
articles.summary: A recent study by cloud storage giant Backblaze has found that nearly 1.5% of all HDDs fail within the first year of operation.
articles.content: A recent study by cloud storage giant Backblaze has shed light on a concerning issue with modern Hard Disk Drives (HDDs). The data reveals that nearly 1.5% of all HDDs fail within a year of operation, with the majority of these failures occurring in the first twelve months. According to Backblaze's analysis of over 350,000 storage drives, roughly 30% of failed HDDs break down without warning, leaving users unaware of any impending issues. This mechanical unpredictability is a significant problem for consumers and businesses alike, as it can lead to data loss and system downtime. The study also highlights the importance of manufacturing quality in determining an HDD's lifespan. Drives from certain manufacturers tend to be more reliable than others, with Seagate emerging as the most mechanically reliable across a recent analysis period. However, even within these brands, there are variations in reliability depending on specific models. Backblaze has been tracking its fleet of storage drives for several years and has developed a detailed understanding of their performance patterns. The company's data shows that HDDs typically last around 807 days before failing, although this figure only accounts for those drives that have already failed. Mechanical failures can be caused by a range of factors, including production defects, accidents such as power surges or drops, and damage to the drive's internal operating system. In some cases, these issues may be apparent through warning signs or error messages, but in many instances, they can occur without any prior indication. The cost-effectiveness of hard disk drives (HDDs) is a major factor contributing to their widespread adoption in data storage solutions. Despite being more prone to mechanical failures than solid-state drives (SSDs), HDDs remain significantly cheaper per gigabyte compared to other storage media. This disparity in pricing is particularly evident in the AI industry, where high-capacity storage is crucial for processing large datasets quickly. As demand for SSD storage continues to rise, driven by AI data centers, prices are increasing accordingly. However, for applications where cost is a top priority, HDDs offer an attractive option due to their lower per-unit costs. The data collected from over 5,000 drives reveals a clear correlation between the age of an HDD and its likelihood of failing. Specifically, the failure rate appears to increase significantly once a drive reaches seven years old. This trend suggests that users who rely on HDDs in their workflow should plan for regular replacements or invest in additional storage solutions. The relatively high failure rates of HDDs are not entirely unexpected, given the mechanical nature of these devices. As such, they can be seen as an inherent characteristic of this technology rather than a flaw. The limitations of current hard drive technology are becoming increasingly apparent as they continue to advance. The majority of drives rely on CMR (Conventional Magnetic Recording) tech, which provides reliable performance but is not without its drawbacks. As HDD manufacturers explore emerging technologies such as SMR and HAMR, it's clear that significant changes are needed to improve the resilience of these devices. Backblaze is keeping a close eye on these developments, although they have yet to incorporate them into their systems. Ultimately, data security requires a multi-layered approach that includes cloud, local, and off-site storage systems to safeguard against loss due to mechanical failure or other calamities. articles.title: Stock Market Selloff Highlights U.S. Debt Burden Fears
articles.summary: A brutal stock selloff last week has shed light on Wall Street's true fears about the growing U.S. debt burden, according to a top economist.
articles.content: A brutal stock selloff last week has shed light on Wall Street's true fears about the growing U.S. debt burden, according to a top economist. The 10-year Treasury yield had been rising sharply before easing in recent weeks as investors sought refuge in government bonds. However, its trajectory was marked by a significant spike of over 100 basis points, pushing it above 5% and reaching its highest level in 24 years at one point. This surge began after the outbreak of war with Iran in late February. The conflict sent oil prices soaring, prompting expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates to combat resurgent inflation. Meanwhile, hyperscalers have been flooding the bond market with fresh debt to finance massive capital expenditures and the AI infrastructure boom. This has sustained a hot economy and sticky inflation. This influx of debt from hyperscalers has competed for investors' dollars as the Treasury Department taps the bond market to finance its $2 trillion budget deficit and service the $40 trillion in U.S. debt. Some analysts have downplayed the spike in yields, attributing it to the crowding out effect caused by AI debt on the U.S. bond market. The recent market downturn has sparked a debate about the true drivers of rising bond yields in the US. According to Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, the past week's selloff provides valuable insights into this issue. Brooks argues that the current market environment is not comparable to the IT bubble of the early 2000s, when corporate borrowing reached unprecedented levels. In contrast, public borrowing is now historically high and more likely driving up yields. The latest jobs report, which showed payrolls growing at a rate double what analysts had expected, also failed to support the argument that AI is responsible for higher yields. The bond market's reaction was particularly telling, with the two-year yield rising more than anticipated by hot economic growth. Brooks points out that the rise in yields following the jobs report cannot be explained solely by the prospect of strong economic growth. This suggests that investors are factoring in risks associated with the trajectory of US debt and deficits. The market-implied yield for a 10-year security 10 years from now is another indicator of these concerns, gauging the premium investors demand to hold Treasuries over the long term. The recent surge in long-term yields has been a major concern for investors and economists alike. One key indicator that suggests fiscal risk is at play is the 10-year10-year forward yield, which measures the market-implied yield for a 10-year security 10 years from now. This metric remained steady despite the decline in both 10-year and two-year yields, indicating that the increase in long-term yields is not solely driven by an AI bubble. In fact, this stability further supports the notion that fiscal risk is the primary driver of the market's concerns. The economist's observation highlights the significance of this indicator. The recent midterm elections and the subsequent sell-off in AI-related stocks have provided a unique opportunity to analyze the underlying factors contributing to rising long-term yields. By isolating these events, experts can better understand what is driving the market's behavior. According to the data, the increase in long-term yields is linked to growing fiscal stress. The federal budget deficit has been widening at an alarming rate, with the Treasury Department reporting a $1.99 trillion gap for fiscal year 2026, a 12% increase from the previous year. Revenue growth of 3% was outpaced by a 6% surge in spending, which is primarily driven by increasing interest payments on the national debt. The US government's growing national debt has led to a significant increase in interest payments, which have surpassed growth in total spending, revenue, and GDP. Net interest payments rose by 8% to $1.05 trillion, outpacing other areas of growth. This surge in interest costs is substantial, equating to approximately $2.9 billion per day. The Peter G. Peterson Foundation estimates that these net interest costs represent a staggering 3.2% of GDP, surpassing the previous record set in 1991. The alarming trend has prompted warnings from experts, who caution that the cycle of higher interest rates and debt could ultimately lead to a catastrophic outcome. Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget President Maya MacGuineas emphasized the urgency of addressing this issue, stating that "there are no easy fixes" and that it cannot be wished away. articles.title: Senegal Migrant Boat Capsizes Off Coast Resulting in 34 Fatalities
articles.summary: At least 34 people are confirmed dead after a migrant boat capsized off the coast of Senegal in the Atlantic Ocean.
articles.content: A migrant boat has capsized off the coast of Senegal in the Atlantic Ocean, resulting in a devastating loss of life. At least 34 people are confirmed dead, according to authorities who have been working to recover bodies from the disaster. The tragedy occurred along one of the most treacherous migration routes in the world, where thousands have perished over the years attempting to reach Spain's Canary Islands from West Africa. The route is notoriously hazardous, with many migrants facing perilous conditions at sea before they even arrive at their destination. Initial reports suggested that 21 bodies had been recovered and only one person was alive after being pulled from the water. However, as rescue efforts continued, the death toll rose to at least 34, according to a statement released by the Senegalese Press Agency (APS). The search for survivors is ongoing, with an "indeterminate number" of people still reported missing. The incident has highlighted the risks faced by migrants attempting to cross the Atlantic Ocean in search of a better life. The incident is being investigated by authorities in Senegal, who are working to locate those still missing and provide support to the families affected. According to Saliou Diouf, founder of Boza Fii, a migrant aid association based in Senegal, the sinking occurred on Friday, contradicting initial reports that it happened on Saturday. The nationalities of all the victims have not been confirmed due to ongoing search efforts. Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has pledged to crack down on people organizing these perilous voyages, vowing to provide hope for young people in the country. He made this commitment through social media posts over the weekend. Thousands of West Africans attempt each year to reach Europe via the treacherous Atlantic route, a journey fraught with risks and uncertainties. Senegalese authorities have made a grim discovery off their coast, where a migrant boat has sunk in the Atlantic Ocean, resulting in at least 34 fatalities. The incident highlights the dangers faced by those attempting to reach Europe via this route. To add complexity to this issue, Senegalese police have intercepted another group of migrants on Friday who were trying to reach Spain on a similar small boat. This group consisted of 23 women, two babies, and two other children from various West African countries, including Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, and Nigeria. The Senegalese interior ministry has stated its determination to combat people smuggling networks by strengthening cooperation with neighboring countries. In a related development, the country's interior minister plans to visit the affected region to meet with families of the victims and express condolences on behalf of the state. In response to the surge in migrant boat arrivals, Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro have declared an emergency, while Senegal, Mauritania, and Morocco have increased maritime patrols around departure points for small boats, forcing them to head further south towards the coasts of Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea. articles.content: Nancy Lacore, the newly elected congresswoman from South Carolina, made history by flipping a seat held by Republicans for 43 out of the last 45 years. Her win was by a narrow margin of just over 3,000 votes. Lacore credits her campaign's focus on building a broad coalition as key to her success. Early on, her team secured an endorsement from a Republican mayor in Mount Pleasant, the largest municipality in the district. This move helped set the tone for reaching out to Independents and moderate Republicans who were crucial to winning the election. As a Democrat, Lacore's background is notable - she was previously registered as a Republican until 2016. Her decision to leave the party was motivated by her disagreement with Donald Trump's policies, but she declined to elaborate further on this aspect of her past. Lacore's campaign strategy was centered around appealing to voters beyond traditional Democratic Party lines. By securing endorsements from within the opposing party and targeting Independents and moderate Republicans, Lacore's team aimed to build a winning coalition that would carry her to victory in a district with a long history of Republican dominance. Lacore's team has been working on building a coalition that would carry her to victory in a district with a long history of bipartisan support. This strategy involves securing endorsements from within the opposing party and targeting Independents and moderate Republicans. The new Congress is expected to have a significant majority, which Lacore believes will provide opportunities for progress on key issues. With many veterans now elected to office, she notes that they tend to focus on achieving their mission rather than being bound by partisan politics. This non-partisan approach could potentially lead to more effective collaboration across party lines. Lacore's campaign promises included reducing the cost of housing, medical care, and healthcare, as well as eliminating tax breaks for data centers. She also plans to address rising costs driven by the ongoing war and tariffs imposed on various goods. The One Big Beautiful Bill has both positive and negative aspects, according to Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore. While she is enthusiastic about provisions that exempt tips and Social Security from taxation, she acknowledges that other parts of the bill have had a detrimental effect on affordability. Lacore emphasized her support for tax breaks, specifically mentioning the exemption of tips and Social Security from taxes as a beneficial aspect of the bill. When asked to clarify her stance on this issue, she confirmed her intention to extend these tax benefits. The imposition of tariffs through executive order has been a contentious issue in Congress, with Rep.-elect Lacore pointing out that they were not authorized by lawmakers. This has led to confusion and debate over who is responsible for the tariffs' implementation. With corruption and cost of living being major concerns among voters, Rep.-elect Lacore stressed the need for unity across party lines on these issues. She noted that Americans are looking for accountability from their leaders, but also want them to address pressing problems without taking drastic measures. The public's desire for accountability is clear, but what does it mean in practice? Rep-elect Nancy Lacore suggests that accountability can take different forms depending on the specific issue at hand. She acknowledges that there are areas where corruption and insider trading have been prevalent. One such area is stock trading by elected officials, a practice that has raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest. Lacore notes that putting rules in place to prevent this type of behavior would be an important step towards greater accountability. By doing so, she aims to restore public trust in government. As the highest-ranking female military officer ever elected to Congress, Lacore brings a unique perspective to Capitol Hill. She will be taking her seat alongside other lawmakers who have not experienced service as high-ranking officers before. In fact, no female admiral or general has ever served in such positions previously. Lacore's own experience with the Navy Reserve is also noteworthy. She was relieved of her position as chief in August 2025 by Secretary Hegseth, who has since announced plans to cut the number of high-ranking officers by 20 percent and end diversity initiatives. articles.title: Dinner Served Early in the US
articles.summary: The timing of meals can have a significant impact on one's circadian rhythms and digestive system, with American dinnertime hours often differing from those of other countries.
articles.content: A common phenomenon for international visitors to the United States is the shock of being served dinner at what they consider an unreasonably early hour. This cultural discrepancy can be particularly disorienting for those who are accustomed to eating their main meal later in the evening. The disparity in dinnertime hours between the US and other countries is a notable characteristic of American culture. While visitors from abroad may struggle to adjust to this earlier schedule, it's not just a matter of personal preference - the timing of meals can have a significant impact on one's circadian rhythms and digestive system. One factor contributing to this peculiarity is the influence of traditional American customs and work patterns. The US has a unique blend of cultural values and lifestyle habits that shape when and how people eat their meals. This includes the widespread practice of eating dinner in the early evening, often between 5pm and 7pm. Social media platforms have also played a role in shaping American dinnertime trends, particularly among younger generations who are influenced by online content and social norms. As a result, earlier evening meals have become increasingly popular, further solidifying the US's reputation for eating dinner at an unusually early hour compared to other countries. The eating habits of Americans show a stark contrast when compared to those of other countries. In many parts of the world, dinner is served much later than the typical 5:00-6:00 pm in the US. This preference for earlier dinner times is reflected in American meal patterns. While breakfast and lunch are often light affairs, dinner takes center stage as the heartiest meal of the day. This is not surprising given that many people rely on a large evening meal to fuel their bodies after a long day. The practice of prioritizing dinner over other meals has significant implications for daily routines. Light breakfasts and lunches mean that Americans tend to feel hungrier earlier in the evening, making them ready to sit down to a big meal sooner rather than later. In contrast, many countries place greater emphasis on lunch as their main meal. This is particularly evident in Mexico, Spain, and numerous South American nations, where longer breaks are taken during the day to accommodate a filling midday meal. As a result, these cultures tend not to feel hungry until much later in the evening. The differences in eating habits between countries highlight the unique characteristics of American food culture. While other nations may enjoy a leisurely lunch and save their largest meal for dinner, Americans have developed a distinct preference that shows no signs of changing. The way people approach meals varies significantly across cultures, and one of the most striking differences is in the timing and size of lunch versus dinner. In many countries, including Mexico and those in South America, lunch is not only eaten earlier but also tends to be the largest meal of the day. This is partly due to the fact that these nations have longer breaks for lunch, allowing workers to take time off from their duties and enjoy a filling meal before returning to work. The American work schedule, which typically runs from 9 am to 5 pm with a brief break for lunch, contributes to the disparity in meal sizes. As a result, people often find themselves rushing through meals during this short window, leaving little room for a substantial dinner later on. Countries that take longer midday breaks are able to enjoy larger lunches without feeling pressured to get back to work immediately, giving them more time to relax and savor their food. The time zones in some countries can significantly impact daily schedules and meal times. In Spain, for example, the late sunset means that people often work during daylight hours, which pushes back their dinner time. This is not just a matter of convenience but also a practical necessity given the later evening hours. The influence of time zone on meal times is also evident in countries like the UK and Australia. These nations have a tradition of taking an afternoon snack called tea time, which serves as a midday break and allows people to delay their evening meal. This scheduling flexibility enables individuals to enjoy larger lunches without feeling rushed back into work. While Americans tend to eat around their work schedules, many other countries work around mealtimes. This approach acknowledges that meals are not just about sustenance but also an essential part of daily life, providing a break from work and allowing people to recharge. Meal times in different countries are often shaped by cultural and practical considerations beyond work schedules alone. Factors such as social norms, family obligations, and even local customs can influence when people choose to eat their main meals, resulting in varying patterns around the world. In many countries around the world, dinner is a leisurely affair that takes place late into the evening. For instance, in France, prime-time TV shows don't start until nearly 9 pm to accommodate the fact that people are still enjoying their meals at this hour. Similarly, Italians prioritize dining as an experience that allows for socializing and bonding with others over good food. This approach is reflected in the time they take to eat dinner, which can stretch into several hours. In contrast, Americans tend to view dinner more pragmatically, often treating it as just another item on their daily schedule. With a packed day of work, school, or other activities, many people are eager to fit in mealtime and get back to their busy lives. The influence of social media is also playing a role in shaping American attitudes towards dinnertime. Influencers are promoting early dinners as a key component of a healthy lifestyle, citing studies that suggest eating three hours before bedtime can improve digestion and sleep. Some Gen Z influencers have even adopted the mantra "dinner by 8, in bed by 9" as a way to prioritize their well-being and maintain a balance between work, rest, and play. The traditional American dinner hour has long been a topic of interest, often drawing comparisons to eating habits in other parts of the world. While some cultures enjoy a late evening meal, Americans tend to prioritize an early dinner, typically between 5pm and 7pm. This preference for earlier meals is largely influenced by societal expectations and work schedules, which can make it challenging to eat later in the day. As a result, many people have adopted routines that accommodate this earlier dinner time, such as winding down with a relaxing evening routine after finishing their meal. This has become an integral part of American culture, reflecting the country's unique lifestyle and values. articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Breaks North American Box Office Records
articles.summary: The Japanese film "Godzilla Minus Zero" opened with $31.6 million in North America, surpassing previous records.
articles.content: A Japanese film has broken records at the North American box office with a massive opening weekend haul of $31.6 million. The film, "Godzilla Minus Zero, is a sequel to 2023's Oscar-winning movie Godzilla Minus One and marks a return to the series' Japanese roots. The success of Godzilla Minus Zero comes at the expense of Warner Bros.' animated The Cat in the Hat movie, which opened with $20.5 million over the weekend, along with an additional $10 million from international markets. The film features voice acting by Bill Hader. The revival of the Godzilla franchise is a significant achievement for director Takashi Yamazaki, who has managed to breathe new life into one of the longest-running movie franchises. The film's success also highlights the growing demand for foreign-language content in North America. Despite this impressive opening, Godzilla Minus Zero still trails behind another notable foreign-language film, 2004's Passion of the Christ, which opened with $83.8 million despite featuring largely Aramaic dialogue. The record-breaking opening of Godzilla Minus Zero has set a new benchmark for live-action films worldwide. With a debut weekend total of $31.6 million in North America, it surpasses the previous mark held by 2004's Hero, which launched with $17.9 million. This milestone is part of a growing trend where international, non-English productions are captivating American audiences at cinemas. The success of Godzilla Minus Zero follows closely on the heels of other foreign-language films that have achieved impressive box office numbers in North America. The Indian epic Ramayana: Rise of a Legend also made its mark over the weekend, achieving the widest North American release for an Indian film to date. With a domestic launch of $8.7 million and a total of $32 million earned in India, this Hindi-language production is the most expensive Indian film ever made. In Japan, Godzilla Minus Zero raked in approximately $17 million over the weekend, while Ramayana: Rise of a Legend was given a global release alongside its American debut. The simultaneous global rollout was built on the idea that audiences worldwide connect with Godzilla and the vision of director Takashi Yamazaki, according to Koji Ueda, president of Toho Global. articles.title: Xbox Series X Offers Affordable Alternative to PS5 Pro
articles.summary: The Xbox Series X provides an affordable option compared to the PlayStation 5 Pro, with a starting price of $750 for its all-digital version.
articles.content: The Xbox Series X stands out as a more affordable option compared to the PlayStation 5 Pro, starting at $750 for its all-digital version. In contrast, the PS5 Pro has seen a significant price hike this year, now costing a substantial $900. While the PS5 Pro boasts superior raw GPU specs and upscaling technology, the Xbox Series X holds its own in terms of overall gameplay performance. However, when it comes to features that go beyond pure performance, Microsoft's console offers some notable advantages. One such advantage is Smart Delivery, a feature that ensures users receive the best available version of a game for their hardware. When purchasing a game on the Xbox Series X, Smart Delivery automatically downloads any updates or added features, such as ray tracing or unlocked frame rates, to maximize performance. This streamlined approach contrasts with the PS5 Pro, which lacks a direct equivalent of Smart Delivery. As a result, users often have to manually choose between different versions of a game when downloading from their library. This can lead to issues with saving and loading games across console generations. Smart Delivery's ability to sync saves across console generations automatically is particularly useful for gamers who upgrade or switch consoles frequently. Without this feature, users may encounter problems with transferring saved data from older consoles. The absence of Smart Delivery on the PS5 Pro highlights one area where Microsoft's console excels in terms of user experience. While the PS5 Pro may be more powerful, its limitations in this regard can make it a less convenient choice for some gamers. Smart Delivery is not the only feature that sets the Xbox Series X apart from the PS5 Pro. Its convenience and flexibility have made it a popular choice among gamers looking for a hassle-free gaming experience. As we delve deeper into the features of the Xbox Series X, it becomes clear that Microsoft's console has more to offer than just raw performance. By focusing on user-friendly features like Smart Delivery, the company aims to provide a more enjoyable and seamless gaming experience for its users. The Xbox Series X still offers a disc drive option, unlike its rival, the PS5 Pro. When the consoles were first released in 2020, having a disc drive was seen as an essential feature, and many gamers had built up physical libraries of games on their previous consoles. While the PS5 also offered a discless model from launch, the Series X initially only came with a drive, making it easier for gamers to use their existing collections. Although a cheaper all-digital variant of the Xbox Series X was introduced in 2024, the option is still available for those who prefer physical media. In contrast, the PS5 Pro does not come with a disc drive out of the box, which means that any physical games purchased for the standard PS5 will no longer be playable. This decision has also led to Sony's announcement that it will stop producing disc-based PS5 games in 2028, making it unlikely that future consoles from the company will feature a disc drive. The Xbox Series X/S features have been widely praised, with one standout being Quick Resume. This innovative technology uses the console's SSD to suspend up to three current-generation games in the background, allowing players to pick up where they left off almost instantly. When using Quick Resume, suspended games are moved to the SSD, enabling seamless transitions between gameplay sessions. This feature is particularly beneficial for single-player gamers who value convenience and speed. However, it may not be suitable for live service games that require a constant internet connection. The Xbox Series X has a distinct advantage over the PlayStation 5 Pro when it comes to resuming games. While the PS5 can suspend one game at a time and resume it later, it's limited to doing so when the console is turned on or in rest mode. In contrast, the Xbox Series X allows players to quickly pick up where they left off with multiple games suspended simultaneously. This feature, known as Quick Resume, significantly enhances convenience for gamers who frequently switch between different titles. One area where the PS5 Pro excels is its processing power and potential features like advanced ray tracing and AI upscaling. However, in terms of HDR standards, it falls short by not supporting Dolby Vision, which many consider to be the best standard available. While the PS5 family does support Dolby Atmos audio, Dolby Vision remains absent for both games and movies. This means that users with TVs capable of displaying Dolby Vision may find themselves unable to take full advantage of its superior picture quality. The Xbox Series X also has a notable limitation when it comes to playing blu-ray discs in Dolby Vision. However, the console does support Dolby Vision for optimized games, resulting in enhanced colors and contrast without requiring manual calibration adjustments. As a major selling point, the Xbox Series X boasts an extensive game library through its Game Pass subscription service. This offers users access to almost every first-party game at launch on the Game Pass Ultimate tier, providing significant value for gamers willing to commit to the service. The Xbox Series X has established itself as a powerhouse in terms of backwards compatibility, allowing users to play a vast array of games from previous console generations on their new hardware. This means that gamers can access and enjoy thousands of titles from the Xbox One, 360, and even original Xbox libraries. One key advantage of this extensive library is that it includes hundreds of games from the Xbox 360 era, which is not available on Sony's PS5 Pro. The inclusion of these older titles provides a significant value proposition for gamers who want to play classic games without having to purchase them individually or wait for years for them to become available through the service. Another benefit of the Xbox Series X's backwards compatibility is that it allows users to seamlessly switch between playing on their console and PC, using the same save data. This offers a high degree of flexibility and convenience, making it easier for gamers to play their favorite titles across multiple platforms. Microsoft has also made significant strides in enhancing older games through features like FPS Boost, Auto HDR, and enhanced resolution. These improvements can breathe new life into classic titles, making them look and feel more modern and polished. In contrast, the PS5 Pro's backwards compatibility is more limited, primarily focusing on PS4 games with some occasional boosts to frame rate and loading times. However, Sony has not prioritized supporting physical copies of older PlayStation consoles like the PS3, PS2, or PS1. The lack of support for these older consoles means that gamers who want to play retro titles are largely out of luck. Furthermore, even when games from older consoles are available on the service, they can only be streamed and not played natively, which may be a problem for those with unreliable network connections. Sony's focus on supporting PS4 games is evident in its efforts to enhance these titles through features like improved graphics and faster loading times. However, this narrow focus means that older PlayStation consoles are largely absent from the service, limiting gamers' options when it comes to playing classic titles. The Xbox Series X boasts an array of features that its rival, the PS5 Pro, currently lacks. One such feature is Microsoft's innovative disc-to-digital licensing program, which enables users to convert their physical games into digital tokens. This program is exclusive to Xbox Series X and Xbox One titles, but for hundreds of supported games, all you need to do is insert a disc once to create the license. Once activated, you can play the game without needing the corresponding disc inserted. The digital license is tied to your Microsoft account rather than the physical disc, which means that selling or lending the disc to someone else will automatically cancel the license. This ensures that users can carry their libraries forward even if future Xbox consoles abandon physical discs altogether. Microsoft's commitment to preserving gamers' collections stands in contrast to Sony's plans to end physical disc production by 2028. The PS5 Pro, which is set to follow suit, currently lacks a similar program for converting physical games into digital tokens. The storage capacity of the two consoles differs significantly, with the PS5 Pro boasting twice as much built-in storage at 2TB compared to the Xbox Series X's 1TB. However, gamers who play AAA titles extensively will eventually hit storage limits on either console. Upgrading storage on the Xbox is a relatively straightforward process that requires inserting an M.2 SSD into the dedicated expansion slot inside the console. This involves removing the faceplate and unscrewing the expansion slot cover to make way for the additional SSD. The process of expanding storage on the PS5 Pro, while doable, is significantly more complicated due to its reliance on a dedicated expansion slot that requires careful handling of the faceplate and internal components. This can be intimidating for users who are not familiar with console modifications. The Xbox Series X offers users an easy way to expand their storage capacity without requiring any technical expertise. To do so, one simply needs to purchase an officially licensed Storage Expansion Card from Seagate or Western Digital and insert it into a slot on the back of the console. This process takes mere seconds to complete and doesn't necessitate the use of specialized tools, making it accessible even to those unfamiliar with console modifications. articles.title: Space Weather Events Can Impact Infrastructure on Earth
articles.summary: A recent study has shed light on the rapid effects of substorms caused by space weather events.
articles.content: Auroras in the sky have long been a breathtaking spectacle for those fortunate enough to witness them. These colorful displays of light rippling across the night sky may seem disconnected from events on Earth's surface, but they are actually part of a larger process known as space weather. Space weather is caused by changes in Earth's space environment resulting from solar activity. This phenomenon has a direct impact on our planet's magnetic field and can influence electric currents that flow through the ground beneath our feet. In fact, these currents have been observed to be strong enough to damage power grids and other technological systems on the surface. Researchers like ourselves are working to understand how space weather affects infrastructure on Earth. Our goal is to identify the connections between solar activity, auroras in the sky, and their impact on our daily lives. By studying this complex relationship, we hope to gain insights into mitigating potential disruptions caused by space weather events. A recent study has shed light on the rapid effects of a specific type of space weather event called a substorm. During such an event, energy is released tens of thousands of miles away from Earth, and its impact can be felt on the ground within minutes. The Earth's magnetic field plays a crucial role in shielding our planet from the solar wind, a stream of charged particles emanating from the sun. However, this protection can be compromised when a coronal mass ejection occurs, releasing a massive cloud of charged particles and magnetic fields into space. When a coronal mass ejection reaches Earth, its interaction with our planet's magnetosphere sets off a chain reaction that can have far-reaching consequences. The magnetosphere is the region surrounding Earth dominated by its own magnetic field, which helps to deflect incoming solar radiation and charged particles. The orientation of the coronal mass ejection's magnetic field is critical in determining the severity of its impact on Earth. If it aligns with our planet's magnetic field on the side facing the sun, it can connect and form a conduit for the solar wind to flow through. This connection causes the magnetic field lines to be stretched out into space behind Earth, forming a long region known as the magnetotail. As the solar wind continues to push against the connected field lines, magnetic energy builds up in the magnetotail until it reaches a critical point. At this stage, the stored energy is released explosively in a process called a substorm, which occurs on the side of Earth facing away from the sun at distances ranging from 28,000 to 40,000 miles. The substorm process continues to unfold as energetic particles travel along Earth's magnetic field lines towards our planet. At altitudes of around 56 to 93 miles above the surface, these particles collide with oxygen and nitrogen atoms in the upper atmosphere. This collision results in the production of glowing aurorae that illuminate the night sky. The same energetic particles also have a significant impact on Earth's upper atmosphere by driving strong electrical currents. Rapid changes in these atmospheric electrical currents can cause Earth's magnetic field at ground level to shift dramatically, leading to fluctuations in the planet's overall magnetic field. These changes can induce electric currents in power lines and transformers. The effects of these induced electric currents can be detrimental to infrastructure, potentially causing damage to transformers and triggering circuit breakers to trip. The sequence of events leading to an aurora is well-defined in observations made by spacecraft. When stretched magnetic field lines on the nightside suddenly reconnect, there's a sudden change in the magnetic field and a burst of charged particles moving towards Earth. This energy release has far-reaching consequences, with effects manifesting within minutes. The timing of these events suggests that the aurora and ground disturbance don't appear simultaneously everywhere. Instead, they begin at lower latitudes before spreading northward over the next 20 to 30 minutes. This indicates a clear progression from one location to another. The response of geomagnetic stations near the affected areas is also noteworthy. Stations just tens or hundreds of miles apart can experience vastly different magnetic swings, with some recording strong variations while others see minimal changes. The disparity in responses depends on several factors, including the strength of currents in Earth's upper atmosphere and local conditions like atmospheric conductivity. Atmospheric conductivity varies depending on sunlight and auroral activity, while ground conductivity is influenced by geology and moisture levels. This variability means that nearby locations can have significantly different responses to the same energy release. Witnessing a spectacular aurora doesn't necessarily mean the surrounding area is experiencing the most intense magnetic disturbances or electric currents. The relationship between the two phenomena is complex and depends on various factors. The historical record shows that space weather poses a significant threat to both space and ground infrastructure. A notable example is the 1989 geomagnetic storm, which caused spectacular auroras as far south as Texas and contributed to the collapse of the Hydro-Québec power system. This incident left over 6 million people without electricity for nearly nine hours on a cold winter night. The Halloween storms of 2003 brought spectacular auroras across Europe, but also had a more sinister impact on the ground. A similar combination occurred during the May 2024 geomagnetic storm, which proved to be the strongest in over two decades. The intense solar activity caused geomagnetically induced currents that stressed the power grid in southern Sweden, forcing a critical transmission link to disconnect and temporarily disrupting the flow of electricity through that part of the grid. Space weather forecasts can provide vital warnings to power grid operators hours before solar activity reaches Earth, giving them crucial time to monitor grid conditions and prepare for possible disruptions. However, the effects of substorms unfold rapidly after the solar wind interacts with Earth's magnetic environment, often on timescales of just minutes. The process is complex and involves an explosive release of magnetic energy tens of thousands of miles away from our planet. This event can have far-reaching consequences, including potential risks to power grids, which can be devastating for communities relying on a stable electricity supply. As the aurora ripples across the night sky, it's worth remembering that this breathtaking spectacle is just one aspect of a larger space weather phenomenon with both beautiful and potentially damaging effects. The aurora borealis, or northern lights, is an awe-inspiring display of colored light that dances across the night sky in polar regions. This spectacle is caused by charged particles from the sun interacting with the Earth's magnetic field and atmosphere. As these particles collide with atoms and molecules in the upper atmosphere, they excite them, releasing energy in the form of light. The resulting colors can range from green to pink to purple, depending on the altitude at which the collision occurs. Ultimately, the aurora is a mesmerizing manifestation of the dynamic relationship between our planet and space weather. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-space-weather-powers-auroras-sky.html

articles.title: Saudi Forces and Houthi Rebels Engage in Escalating Conflict
articles.summary: A regional response is being prepared by Syria, which will send its fighters to support Saudi Arabia along their shared border.
articles.content: Fighting between Saudi-backed forces and Houthi rebels in Yemen has reached new heights this summer, prompting a regional response from Syria. Syria is preparing to send its fighters to support Saudi Arabia along their shared border, according to three officials familiar with the plans. The deployment would mark a significant escalation of the conflict in Yemen, which began in February when US and Israeli forces targeted Iranian interests. Regional officials have confirmed that Syrian military advisers are already present in Saudi Arabia, but no combat troops have been sent to Yemen yet. The exact timing and scope of the planned deployment remain unclear, with details only shared on a need-to-know basis. The conflict in Yemen has seen both sides exchange blows, with Houthi rebels launching attacks on Saudi territory in recent months. Despite having access to advanced US-supplied fighter jets and missile defense systems, Saudi Arabia has struggled to gain the upper hand against the Houthis. Syria's decision to intervene in the conflict is likely driven by its own security concerns, given its long history of civil war and battle-hardened fighters. The move could potentially reshape the balance of power in the region, with significant implications for regional stability. The Syrian government has agreed to send troops to support Saudi Arabia in its conflict with the Houthi rebels, a move that could significantly alter the regional balance of power. A senior Syrian official confirmed that an initial contingent of around 600 special forces fighters is set to arrive in Saudi Arabia within the next week. This deployment marks a significant escalation of Syria's involvement in the conflict, which has been marked by its support for various rebel groups during the country's own civil war. In recent weeks, a high-ranking delegation led by Khaled Khattab, commander of the 82nd Division, visited Saudi Arabia to discuss the terms of the agreement. The delegation received briefings on the current state of the conflict and was reportedly informed about the areas of operation where Syrian troops would be deployed. Syria has already begun providing military advisers to Saudi Arabia, with a small number of officials currently stationed in the kingdom to assist in training Yemeni forces. Syrian officials have revealed that their country is in talks to join a defense agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan last August. The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement commits these countries to consider an attack on one of them as an attack on all three, and to strengthen military cooperation. Discussions about Syria's potential membership are reportedly at an advanced stage, although no official announcement has been made yet. The agreement would see Syria align its defense policies with those of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, creating a united front against external threats. However, one concern is that Syria might seek support from these countries to counter Israel's actions in southern Syria. After President Bashar Assad was ousted in December 2024, Israeli forces took control of a U.N.-patrolled buffer zone and have occupied it since. Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa has stated that his government does not aim to escalate tensions with Israel and has called for the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the buffer zone. This stance is significant, as the Syrian president's administration has been working closely with Saudi Arabia in recent weeks. The two countries announced a military cooperation agreement last week, without providing further details. During President al-Sharaa's visit to Riyadh, the Saudi government agreed to provide Syria with over $400 million to fund post-conflict reconstruction efforts, including rebuilding homes and basic infrastructure. This financial support is seen as a key component of the emerging partnership between Syria and Saudi Arabia. Syria's decision to reject US President Donald Trump's proposal for its forces to intervene against Hezbollah in Lebanon is a reflection of its current priorities. The country is focused on rebuilding and recovering from its devastating civil war, which has left deep scars. The relationship between Syria and Saudi Arabia has undergone significant changes in recent times. Under Assad's rule, Syria was largely isolated by the Arab world. However, with Saudi Arabia's support, Syria is now being reintegrated into the region. Syrian involvement in the conflict against the Houthis in Yemen would expose it to potential attacks from allied militias in neighboring Iraq. This is a concern for Syria as it seeks to rebuild and stabilize its country without getting entangled in new conflicts. The emerging partnership between Syria and Saudi Arabia has been bolstered by financial support, which is seen as crucial to their growing cooperation. articles.title: iPhones Offer Up to 2TB Storage Capacity
articles.summary: The latest iPhones offer internal storage capacities of up to 2TB, but most users may not need such a large amount.
articles.content: The latest smartphones have been equipped with massive storage capacities, including some models that boast an impressive 2TB of internal space. While this may sound like a luxury worth splurging on, it's essential to consider whether such a large capacity is truly necessary for most users. Apple's high-end iPhones are a prime example of this phenomenon. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 with 256GB of storage, but the price doubles when opting for the 2TB model. Similarly, the iPhone Duo's base model costs $1,999 with 256GB storage, and jumps to an eye-watering $3,199 with 2TB. For most individuals, a more modest storage capacity is sufficient for their daily needs. With photos automatically syncing to the cloud, streaming services replacing traditional media downloads, and social apps taking up less space than before, there's little justification for investing in a 2TB phone. Unless you have specific requirements that necessitate such an enormous storage capacity - such as shooting professional-grade videos or editing long-form content - it may be wise to opt for a more affordable model with a lower storage capacity. The existence of a 2TB iPhone storage option may seem excessive, but it's actually a necessity for certain types of content creators. These individuals, who rely on their iPhones to capture high-quality images and videos, require ample storage space to accommodate their extensive libraries. For instance, photographers shooting ProRes RAW video can quickly consume up to 100GB of storage per ten-minute take. This is because each minute of footage can occupy over 10GB, with the highest quality setting reaching upwards of 15GB per minute. As a result, serious content creators require at least 1TB of storage to manage their work efficiently. In addition to content creation, gamers also benefit from the 2TB option. Games themselves may not be massive in size, but when combined with multiple game saves and other data, they can quickly add up to over 100GB of storage. This is why gaming enthusiasts who want to store large collections of games on their iPhone appreciate the extra storage capacity. Furthermore, individuals who prefer to keep their personal files private may also find value in the 2TB option. By storing their photos and videos locally rather than syncing them with iCloud, they can maintain greater control over their data and avoid relying on cloud services for storage. For individuals who require a significant amount of storage on their phone, 2TB may seem excessive at first glance. However, professionals such as photographers and video editors often need large amounts of space to store and manage their work. Photographers working with RAW files face the challenge of dealing with massive file sizes - up to 10 times larger than compressed JPEGs. This can quickly consume a phone's storage capacity, especially if they're maintaining a library of original images. Video editors also require ample storage for editing footage directly on their device without constant file management. For those who enjoy downloading movies and shows for travel, a significant amount of storage is required. A single film can take up 3GB to 4GB of space, so even a modest collection of titles can quickly fill a phone's capacity. The need for local storage becomes even more pressing when working in remote locations or areas with poor connectivity. In such situations, relying solely on cloud services for storage can be limiting, as files may not be able to be uploaded or transferred in real-time. When deciding how much storage is needed, it's essential to consider the intended use of the phone and the types of files that will be stored. This helps to ensure that there's enough room for all necessary content, without relying too heavily on cloud services. For individuals who use their phone moderately, 128 or 256GB of internal storage may be sufficient. This is because they typically take a small number of photos daily and install only essential apps, while occasionally streaming content and playing casual games. Power users, such as gamers, require more space to store their extensive collections of apps and games. Pro creators also need substantial storage capacity, especially if they rely on their phones for work, as 1TB or 2TB models provide the necessary room without needing external storage solutions. articles.title: Sharp Decline Expected in Stock Market Values Due to AI Investment Slowdown
articles.summary: Investors are expected to face further losses as the AI investment boom begins to slow down due to a decline in revenue generated from external customers.
articles.content: A sharp decline in stock market values is expected to continue, with investors facing further losses as the AI investment boom begins to slow down, according to a warning from Capital Economics. The slowdown in AI investment will be triggered by a decline in revenue generated from external customers, which would need to increase by 10-fold by 2030 to justify the massive spending. While it's possible for revenues to surge at such a rapid rate, it implies a significant disruption to existing businesses and labor markets. A handful of leading technology companies are expected to invest around $800 billion this year, more than double their investment from last year, with an estimated increase in spending to over $1 trillion by 2027. However, these forecasts assume that annual capital expenditures will remain above the $1 trillion mark for several years. To justify such high levels of spending, AI-related revenues would need to experience a massive surge, which is currently unlikely given the pace of economic disruption seen so far. The possibility of a rapid and severe disruption to existing businesses and labor markets makes it difficult to predict how quickly revenue will grow. The economist predicts that investment in AI will continue to rise next year but at a slower rate, followed by a sharp decline in 2028, with an estimated drop of around 10%. The economist's forecast for a slowdown in AI investment is expected to have a ripple effect on other economies that are heavily reliant on technology. Taiwan and South Korea, two Asian countries with significant tech industries, may see their real GDP growth decline by 3% and 1%, respectively, next year, compared to previous estimates. The stock market is also likely to feel the impact of the impending AI investment downturn. Redwood predicts that the S&P 500 index will be 12% lower than its current level by the end of 2027, down from a peak in early October. This decline could be even more pronounced for tech-heavy indices. A drop in financial markets can have far-reaching consequences for the economy. According to Redwood, higher energy prices or changes in term premia could make it harder for companies to access financing, exacerbating the economic downturn. The wealth effect, which drives consumer spending, will also come under pressure as stock prices fall. The decline in AI investment is expected to have a significant impact on GDP growth rates. Redwood estimates that the market's rally over the past year has contributed around 0.4% to GDP growth, and a selloff could have a similar drag on the economy. This highlights the interconnectedness of financial markets and economic performance. Despite the economist's dire predictions for AI investment, the technology itself is expected to continue driving productivity improvements in the coming years. The existing infrastructure and new investments will help spread the benefits of AI across various industries, even if at a slower pace than previously anticipated. The economist expects a slowdown in GDP growth for the US economy in 2028, but not a major downturn. While there is a risk of recession following a capex boom and bust, a decline in capital spending alone has typically been insufficient to cause one. Despite the impending slowdown in AI investment, Redwood predicts that adoption will continue to expand, driving productivity gains and supporting output growth. She estimates that AI will increase US productivity by around 1% per year for several years, a boost that will contribute to sustained economic expansion. The shift towards a more sustainable pace of AI investment is expected to occur gradually, with sufficient capacity still being added to support continued growth in AI usage. This adjustment should help mitigate the impact of the slowdown on the economy, ensuring that any downturn remains mild and manageable. articles.content: A hidden gem nestled in Southern Italy's Calabria region is the church of St. Nicholas of Platea in Scalea, a place where locals and visitors alike can find solace and connection to their faith. The Parish of St. Nicholas of Platea has been led by one dedicated priest for 30 years: Don Giacomo. In Italian culture, 'Don' is a term used to address priests, short for the Latin word 'Dominus,' meaning lord or father. Located in Scalea, in the Province of Cosenza, this sacred sanctuary is home to the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Lauro. The historic structure has a rich history, dating back to medieval times before 1100, with a crypt beneath the current church that houses columns from a Roman temple and frescoes from the 1400s. The crypt is a testament to the region's rich past, showcasing remnants of ancient civilizations. In contrast, the church above is a beautifully designed place of worship, featuring a stunning dedication to Our Lady of Mount Carmel, painted by Azzolino in the 1700s. Don Giacomo has been the priest at St. Nicholas of Platea for three decades, guiding his community through life's joys and challenges. His dedication to the parish is evident in the care he takes to preserve its history and traditions. The church's architecture is a blend of styles, with the medieval crypt beneath the current structure adding an air of mystique to the overall design. The frescoes in the crypt are particularly noteworthy, dating back to the 1400s and providing a glimpse into the artistic tastes of the time. articles.title: Ina Garten's Brown-Butter Skillet Cornbread Recipe a Crowd-Pleaser for Holidays
articles.summary: This cornbread recipe is a staple at holiday gatherings due to its perfect balance of sweet and savory flavors.
articles.content: I recall trying Ina Garten's easy cornbread recipe several years ago and being thoroughly impressed by its simplicity and flavor. Since then, I've made it for every Thanksgiving gathering, as it never fails to be a crowd-pleaser. The combination of sweet and savory flavors is perfectly balanced, making each bite a delight. Garten's brown-butter skillet cornbread was a hit at our Friendsgiving celebration years ago, and it has since become an essential part of my holiday cooking routine. I always look forward to making this dish for family and friends. When planning the menu for a recent Friendsgiving gathering, I knew I had to include some of Ina Garten's signature recipes. Her overnight mac and cheese was another must-try, as well as her Parmesan smashed potatoes, no Thanksgiving table is complete without carbs, after all. To make Garten's brown-butter skillet cornbread, which serves 10 to 12 people, you'll need just a few basic ingredients: 3 cups of all-purpose flour, 2 cups of whole milk, 1 cup of fine cornmeal (Garten recommends this for moister cornbread), 1 cup of sugar, and ½ pound of unsalted butter. The mixture of butter and milk was whisked together in a bowl before adding two eggs. The eggs were cracked into the bowl without being lightly beaten first, but it didn't seem to affect the final product. In another bowl, the dry ingredients were combined: 3 cups of all-purpose flour, 1 cup of fine cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, and kosher salt. These ingredients were whisked together before making a well in the center of the mixture. The wet butter-and-milk mixture was then poured into the well created by the dry ingredients. The mixture was stirred just until it was combined, with Garten emphasizing that lumps are okay at this stage. Before proceeding to the next step, the batter needed some time to rest and allow the ingredients to meld together. According to Garten's recipe, this resting period is crucial for achieving the best cornbread results. After pouring the batter into the skillet, it's essential not to wipe out any remaining butter residue. This can be easily done by simply throwing the batter right in, without worrying about cleaning the pan first. The cast-iron skillet is then placed in the oven for a specified baking time of 35 to 40 minutes at 350 degrees Fahrenheit, as per Garten's recipe. However, it's worth noting that if you're using an 11 ½-inch skillet, the recommended baking time is reduced to 25 to 30 minutes. After the initial baking time has passed, a knife is inserted into the middle of the cornbread to check for doneness. If the knife comes out clean, as was the case in this instance, it's clear that the cornbread is ready. The finished product proved to be a stunning golden brown, making it an ideal centerpiece for any Thanksgiving table. The cornbread's texture was nothing short of impressive - moist and fluffy, with a perfect balance of sweet and savory flavors that complemented each other beautifully. Despite being stuffed to capacity, everyone at the table couldn't resist going back for seconds, a testament to the recipe's undeniable appeal. Garten's brown-butter skillet cornbread had clearly stolen the show, earning rave reviews from all who tasted it. In October, a British Airways flight was forced to make an emergency landing after a passenger's device caught fire, causing significant concern among travelers. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has reported a staggering 28 battery fire events on passenger and cargo planes in the first quarter of this year alone. If this trend continues, it is likely to surpass last year's record of 97 events, which itself was an increase from 89 incidents in 2024. This surge in battery-related fires poses a significant threat to air travel safety. The FAA has been tracking these incidents closely, and the numbers are alarming. With more devices relying on batteries than ever before, it is essential for passengers to be aware of the risks involved and take necessary precautions. The enclosed space of an airplane makes fires particularly hazardous, making it crucial for travelers to pack their devices safely. Any battery can potentially start a fire if not stored correctly, but lithium metal (non-rechargeable) and lithium-ion (rechargeable) batteries are considered the biggest threats. As air travel becomes increasingly dependent on portable electronics, understanding how to pack these devices safely is essential for preventing such incidents from occurring in the future. Lithium batteries have become increasingly popular over recent years due to their compact size and long-lasting power. However, this surge in demand has also led to an increased risk of thermal runaway, a self-sustaining chemical reaction that produces extreme heat, toxic smoke, ultrafine particles, and flames within seconds. This can happen unexpectedly due to various factors such as damage to the battery, overheating, overcharging, exposure to water, or manufacturing defects. The resulting lithium battery fires are notoriously difficult for cabin crews to extinguish using traditional methods. Lithium batteries are commonly found in a range of portable electronics, including cell phones, laptops, vapes, and power banks. These devices have been linked to several aircraft incidents, with notable cases involving a laptop battery fire on an American Airlines plane in 2024 that injured three passengers. A similar emergency occurred on a Virgin Australia flight in 2025 when a power bank caught fire. In addition to power banks, other devices that contain lithium batteries pose a risk during air travel. These include wireless earbuds and noise-canceling headphones, which are commonly used by passengers. Some electronic devices, such as cameras and drones, also contain lithium batteries. To determine whether your device has a lithium battery, check the label or manual for specific information. For coin-cell batteries, the label will typically start with "CR" if lithium is involved. This is an essential step in understanding the regulations surrounding lithium batteries during air travel. The size of the lithium battery and its installation in a device also play a crucial role in determining the regulations that apply. Non-rechargeable batteries are limited to 2 grams of lithium per battery, while rechargeable batteries have a rating limit of 100 watt hours. This distinction is critical for travelers who want to pack their devices safely. The rules governing lithium batteries can be confusing, but being aware of these limitations is essential for avoiding any issues during air travel. By understanding the regulations and taking necessary precautions, passengers can ensure a safe and smooth journey. When it comes to packing larger batteries for air travel, approval from the airline is required. Spare or uninstalled lithium batteries, including power banks and cell phone charging cases, are prohibited in checked baggage by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). These must be carried in a passenger's carry-on luggage instead. If a gate-check is necessary, passengers must remove these types of batteries from their bags and keep them with them throughout the flight. This ensures that they remain within easy access at all times. Additionally, lithium batteries contained within devices can usually be packed in checked baggage as long as the device is fully powered off to prevent accidental activation. When packing batteries for travel, it's essential to know which types are allowed in checked and carry-on bags. Dry batteries such as AAs, button cells, and 9-volts can be safely packed in both categories. To keep batteries secure during transit, consider storing them in their original packaging or a protective case. This can include the battery pocket of a camera bag or even a plastic baggy. These precautions help prevent accidental activation and potential damage to surrounding items. It's worth noting that rechargeable batteries should not be packed with their charging units. Instead, store them separately to avoid any potential issues during travel. This simple step can make a significant difference in maintaining the safety of your luggage. During a flight, being aware of lithium battery safety is crucial. If you notice a device overheating or smoking, alert the crew immediately. Additionally, if you drop a lithium battery-containing device between seats, notify a crew member promptly to ensure a swift response in case of an emergency. Travelers who fail to adhere to battery-packing guidelines may face significant fines, but more critically, they also put others at risk on their flight. To avoid such consequences and ensure a trouble-free journey, it is essential to follow the recommended packing practices for lithium batteries and devices as outlined earlier in this article. Additionally, being mindful of your surroundings during flights can help prevent accidents, such as dropping a device containing lithium batteries between seats. By taking these precautions, travelers can minimize risks associated with battery-related incidents on planes, ultimately contributing to a safer travel experience for everyone involved. articles.title: US Department of Defense Unveils Plan to Create War Stockpile on American Soil
articles.summary: The plan aims to ensure the country's military capabilities remain intact in the event of cyberattacks and sabotage that disrupt domestic factories and power grids.
articles.content: The US Department of Defense has unveiled plans to create a war stockpile on American soil, aimed at ensuring the country's military capabilities remain intact even in the event of cyberattacks and sabotage that disrupt domestic factories and power grids. At the heart of this initiative is the need for critical minerals, fuel, and munitions. However, experts warn that securing these resources may prove to be a significant challenge. The US currently produces less than 1% of one of the most common types of rare-earth magnets used by its military. The country's reliance on foreign suppliers, particularly China, which dominates processing for many critical minerals, has also raised concerns. China has been known to limit American companies' access to these resources even in times of peace. This vulnerability could have far-reaching implications for US military operations if a conflict were to occur. The FORTRESS America initiative was formally established on September 30th and is designed to enable US forces to continue operating even if domestic power grids and manufacturing supply chains are disrupted. The program builds on earlier efforts to ensure military bases can function without the grid for up to 90 days, and its planned scale is being described as unprecedented in recent history. The Pentagon's plan to stockpile war materials within the US is facing a significant challenge due to America's reliance on foreign supply chains for critical minerals. Clark noted that during the Cold War, the military stored large quantities of war matériel overseas near potential battlefields in Eastern Europe or Northeast Asia. However, FORTRESS focuses on safeguarding supplies within the country, reflecting concerns that American factories could become targets due to cyber threats, drone attacks, electromagnetic warfare, and insider attacks. China's capabilities in these areas are a major concern for US officials, who warn that Beijing could disrupt industrial production through various means. In fact, U.S. agencies have already identified Chinese state-sponsored hackers infiltrating critical infrastructure within the country. The US defense industry is heavily reliant on foreign supply chains for its raw materials, with over $60 billion worth of critical minerals other than rare earths imported in 2025 alone. The US military's reliance on rare-earth magnets has become a major concern, with domestic sources struggling to meet demand. According to recent data, the country's most common type of rare-earth magnet is in short supply, with only 300 metric tons produced domestically in 2025 compared to a staggering 48,000 metric tons in demand. The shortage is already having real-world consequences, as major companies like Ford are feeling its effects on their factory floors. In May 2025, the automaker was forced to idle one of its Chicago plants for a week due to a lack of rare-earth supplies. This is just one example of how the supply chain disruptions are impacting American industry. China's tightening export controls have only added to the problem, making it increasingly difficult for US companies to secure enough rare-earth materials. Despite repeated calls from US officials for China to fulfill its commitments on rare earths and other critical minerals, Beijing has shown no signs of easing up on restrictions. The Pentagon is well aware of the risks posed by foreign dependence on these critical supplies, particularly in a major war scenario where shipping routes and overseas production could be severely disrupted. In an effort to reduce reliance on foreign sources, the military is pursuing a dual strategy that involves building raw-material reserves while investing in domestic mining and processing capacity. The US military's efforts to build a war stockpile are facing significant challenges in securing essential minerals. Tungsten is one such metal where the country's reliance on imports has become increasingly problematic. The last time domestic production of tungsten was commercially viable was 2015, when cheaper imported supplies undercut local output. According to the US Geological Survey, the nation's net import reliance for tungsten exceeded 50% in 2025, highlighting the pressing need for a reliable domestic supply chain. This issue has been exacerbated by the fact that no new tungsten mines have come online since the last one closed. A recent contract awarded to The Elmet Group, a leading tungsten manufacturer, is intended to alleviate some of these concerns. Under the terms of the deal, worth up to $2 billion, Elmet will supply tungsten ores, concentrates, and sodium tungstate to the National Defense Stockpile. However, delivery of these supplies has been put on hold until new production capacity comes online from investments made in Nevada, Australia, and Spain. The US Department of Defense's ambitious plan to stockpile critical minerals has hit a significant roadblock. Analysts are warning that achieving supply chain independence will take time, citing the complexity of rapidly building both finished products and raw mineral reserves. According to experts, the Pentagon is unlikely to meet its goals in the near term due to structural difficulties. Building the necessary infrastructure to compete with China's dominant supply chain will require significant investment and a substantial amount of time. The first test for the US defense industry comes soon, as new federal regulations set to take effect from January 1, 2027, will prohibit defense contractors from purchasing rare earths, magnets, and tungsten from countries including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, unless they can source these materials domestically.
